description: Ready-to-run Docker images containing Jupyter applications

summary.one_liner: A set of ready-to-run Docker images from the Jupyter project that bundle JupyterLab, Jupyter Notebook, and common interactive computing tools.
summary.what_it_does: Provides prebuilt Docker stack images (for example base-notebook, scipy-notebook, datascience-notebook, pytorch-notebook, tensorflow-notebook) published to the Quay.io registry. Running a stack image starts a Jupyter Server with the JupyterLab frontend by default, which is reachable through a port mapped from the container with a secret token printed in the console. Users can mount a host directory into the container to keep work files, and can switch the frontend to classic Jupyter Notebook via the DOCKER_STACKS_JUPYTER_CMD environment variable. Images are published for both x86_64 and aarch64, with some CUDA-enabled variants of the PyTorch and TensorFlow images. The README also documents older images tagged by Ubuntu and Python version, and points to documentation for JupyterHub use and building custom project Dockerfiles.
use_cases: Run a personal JupyterLab server in a container
Serve JupyterLab to a team through JupyterHub
Start a disposable notebook environment with a mounted work folder
Get a preconfigured Python data science environment without local installs
Use GPU-enabled PyTorch or TensorFlow notebooks
Base image for writing a custom project Dockerfile
notable: Multiple prebuilt images targeting different needs (base, scipy, datascience, pytorch, tensorflow, and others), all from one project
Switch between JupyterLab and classic Notebook at container startup with an environment variable
Multi-platform builds for x86_64 and aarch64, plus CUDA variants for PyTorch and TensorFlow
Older Ubuntu and Python combinations remain available as pinned image tags
caveats: Images are only pushed to Quay.io since 2023-10-20; Docker Hub copies are no longer updated
Only one set of images is built at a time; the weekly latest tag tracks Ubuntu 26.04 and Python 3.13, so older environments need pinned tags
tensorflow-notebook is not published as a multi-platform image in the early 2022 policy, and CUDA variants are limited to specific platforms
